1. (1) This Act may be cited as the Accountants Act, 1967.

(2) This Act shall apply throughout the Federation and
shall come into operation on such date as the Minister may

by notification in 8 appoint.

(3) The Minister may by notification in the Gazette
suspend the operation of this Act in any part of the

Federation.

2. In this Act, unless the context otherwisé requires—

"Committee" means any Committee established under
this Act;

"Council" means the Council of the Institute;

"Institute" means the Malaysian Institute of Accountants
established by section 3;

"Member" means a member of the Institute who is
registered in accordance with the provisions of this Act as a
public accountant, registered accountant of licensed
accountant;

"Minister" means the Minister charged with the responsi-
bility for finance;

"register" means the  pogiatar  of members required to
be kept in accordance with the provisions of section 16;

"Registrar" means the Registrar appointed under the
provisions of section 15;

"rules" means rules made under this Act.

powers,    corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal,

(2). Without prejudice to the generality of sub-section (1),
the Institute shall have power to do all acts as are necessaty

(a) to purchase or lease any lands required for anyof
the purposes of the! Institute;

(b) to take up and subscribe for or otherwise acquire

company is essential or  advantageous  to the

to sell, surrender, lease, exchange or mortgage
any land or building vested in it in such manner

(d) to borrow money whether by way of bank over-

(e) to guarantee any contract with any company from

lease or tenancy in accordance with the provisions
of paragraph (b) and any other contract in which

Which it may lawfully be a party in accordance

Part II
THE COUNCIL

8. (1) For the purposes of this Act there shall be established
a Council of the Institute consisting of the following:

(a) the Accountant-General of the Federation or his
_ nominee;

(b) (event public accountants to be elected by members
att? are public accountants; and

(c) sx "six registered acco oe to be elected by members
who are registered accountants.

(2) The President and Vice-President of the Institute shall
be elected by the Council from amongst its members and
in the event of any casual vacancy arising in respect of the
office of the President or of the Vice-President, the Council
shall at its next meeting or as soon as may be thereafter
elect one of its members to fill such vacaincy.

(3) The provisions of the First Schedule shall have effect

9! The Institute and its funds shall be managed by the
Council and all such powers, acts of things as may be

Provided that no resolution of the Institute shall invali-
date the exercise of any power or the doing of any act or
thing by the Council previously which would have been
valid if such resolution had not been passed.

10. Without prejudice to the generality of section 9 and
subject to rules, the Council shall have power—

(a) to make by-laws to, provide for all matters not

its powers or not and by-laws for the inculcation

able practices of that profession and the promotion

(b) to appoint at its discretion such officers, clerks,
agents and servants for permanent, temporary or
special services as it may deem fit and to
determine their duties and terms and conditions
of service;

(c) to take cognisance of anything affecting the Insti-
tute or the professional conduct of its members

purpose of obtaining and communicating infor-
mation on all matters likely to prove beneficial
or interesting to members and to negotiate and
arrange with  such bodies for the reciprocal
recognition of the status of the members: of the

11. (1) Notwithstanding the| provisions of section 7 and

(2) All rules made under sub-section (1) shall require the

Part IV
MEMBERSHIP OF THE INSTITUTE

12. (1) Subject to the provisions of sub-sections (3) and (4)
every person on payment of the prescribed fee shall be
entitled to be admitted as a member of the Institute, if—

(a) he has passed such examinations as are prescribed
in Part I of the Second Schedule; or

(b) he is a member of one of the associations of
accountants included in Part II of the Second
Schedule.

(2) For the purposes of paragraph (a) of sub-section (1) a
person shall be deemed to have passed the examinations
referred to in that paragraph if he has passed an examina-
tion or part of an examination (whether in the Federation
or elsewhere) which is recognised by the Institute as being
equivalent to or higher than the examinations or part
thereof first mentioned in this sub-section.

13. (1) An applicant shall, before admission as a public
accountant, satisfy the Council that he has had—

(a) not less than five years' experience in the office of
a public accountant or of a practisiig accountant
overseas who is a member of one of the recognised
bodies listed in Part II of the Second Schedule;

(b) in the case of an applicamt who has a degree of a
University or Institution! approved by the associa-
tion of which he is a member, not less than three
years' experience as spetified in paragraph (a) of
this sub-section;

(c) after qualifying, not less than three years' experience
as specified in paragraph (a) of this sub-section; or

(d) authority under sub-section (6) of section 8 of the
Companies Act, 1965, tolact as a company auditor
without limitation' or conditions.

(2) An applicant shall, before ddmission as a registered
accountant, satisfy the Council that he has had—

(a) not less than five years' practical accounting
experience in the service of a public accountant,
Government department, bank, insurance com-
pany, local authority or other commercial, finan-
cial, industrial, or professional organisation or
other undertaking approved by the Council;

(b) in the case of an applicant who has a degree of a
University or Institution|approved by the associa-
tion of which he is a member, not less than three
years' experience as specified in paragraph (a) of
this sub-section; or

(c) after qualifying, not less than three years' experience
as specified in paragraph (a) of this sub-section.

(3) For the purpose of this sedtion "qualifying" means
qualifying for membership of the Institute in accordance
with section 12 (1).

of section 12 every person om payment of the prescribed fee

(2) A licensed accountant admitted under this section
shall be subject to the same restrictions, limitations or
conditions as have been imposed upon him under the
Companies Act, 1965.

(3) A licensed accountant|who has been certified by the
Council acting on a report by a Committee appointed under
the provisions of rules as fit to be admitted as a public
accountant or a registered accountant, shall be entitled to be
admitted as such.

PART V
REGISTRATION OF ACCOUNTANTS

15. For the purpose of this Act the Institute shall with the
approval of the Minister appoint a Registrar who shall

exercise and discharge the functions conferred or imposed
on him by this Act or any rules.

16. (1) The Registrar shall maintain a register of members
in which the members shall be classified as—

(a) public accountants;

(b) registered accountants; and

(c) licensed scoot

shall make it available for inspection at reasonable hours

GENERAL.

19, At the first meeting of the Council held after the first
general meeting and after each annual general meeting of
the Institute, the Council] shall appoint the following
Committees :
(a) an Investigation Committee comprising three mem-
bers of the Coungil of whom two shall form a

quorum; and.

(b) a Disciplinary Committee comprising five members

of the Council not} being members of the Investi-

gation Committee] of whom three shall form a

quorum.

20. (1) The Investigation Committee shall investigate any
complaints made against any member in the manner laid
down in the rules and where iit considers that this is justified
shall refer the matter to the Disciplinary Committee.

(2) The Disciplinary Corhmittee shall if it thinks fit
exercise in respect of such member any disciplinary powers
conferred upon it by rules.

21. (1) Any member aggrieved by any decision of the
Disciplinary Committee may) within a period of twenty-one
days after such decision has been communicated to him,
appeal to the High Court.

(2) The procedure governing such appeals to the High
Court shall be the same as for appeals to the High Court
from decisions of a subordinate court in civil matters.

24. Nothing in section 22 or section 23 shall debar any
